findings.label: Suppliers with Current Red Flags
findings.detail: 8 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)

findings.label: Likely Duplicate Payments
findings.detail: 456 high-confidence duplicate groups with same supplier, amount, date and reference (3+ copies) (after filtering 3386 CSV republication artifacts)
findings.context_note: Quarterly CSV overlaps (same transaction appearing in 2 files) have been filtered out. Remaining duplicates show 3+ identical copies, which are more likely genuine overpayments.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 76 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 204 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Britannia Radio Cars Merseyside Ltd (4.0 day avg, 29 payments, £18.8K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Analysis
findings.detail: Digit distribution across 40,838 transactions shows χ²=312.22 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 1.3% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 40,838+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (1.3%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 47,610 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 2.77% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=47,610.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 21 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: GB-St Helens: TPPL St Helens Council NEPO HGV Lot  (£2.6M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

key_findings.title: 5 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Britannia Radio Cars Merseyside Ltd — every 4.0 days (29 payments, £18.8K)

key_findings.title: MATRIX SCM LTD: 2118 transactions totalling £3.8M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.8K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: 2 service categories with a single supplier
key_findings.description: Top: Multevo Limited — sole winner in 'Utility vehicles' (2 contracts, £312.6K). Category monopolies may indicate market failure or specification bias.
